chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Maymun, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man was affected by janabah during the night, so he performed ghusl and offered salat. Then when morning came, he looked and found janabah on his garment. He said: “All praise belongs to Allah, Who has not left anything without appointing a limit for it. If, at the place where he stood, he had not looked, then repeating is upon him.”

I wrote to Abi al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام asking him about a castrated man who urinates and faces hardship from that, and then sees moisture after moisture. He said: “He performs wudu (ablution) and sprinkles his garment once during the day.”

key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act, here meaning repeating the prayer
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment, whose purity affects the validity of salat
key_terms.فَاغْتَسَلَ: he performed ghusl for ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if janabah is found on one’s garment after ghusl and salat, or if moisture continues after urination?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings related to ritual purity, specifically janabah on clothing and recurrent moisture after urination. It shows that the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام gave precise legal boundaries for cases of hardship and impurity affecting salat and garments.
